clue.text: Mark mobile soldiers' second uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Armoured Corps, is the British Army's mobile tank arm

explanation.surface: A wound left by a rebellion among armoured troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns RACS (RAC plus S) upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting trace a wound leaves on the skin, a kind of mark.

clue.text: Rings one set aside at the beginning

indicators.note: says the piece for 'set aside' goes at the front, ahead of the piece for 'one'

parts.note: to annul a ruling is to set it aside
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rings, one of them put aside right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'one' + 'set aside at the beginning': the annulling word comes first, then I.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the Latin plural of annulus, a ring-shaped figure or part.

clue.text: Scientist testing ice melting

indicators.note: melting ice loses its shape, so the letters of the two words run into a new order

explanation.surface: A researcher running experiments on melting ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A geneticist is a scientist who studies genes and heredity.

clue.text: Sailor has bath outside in river

indicators.note: the bath word goes outside, wrapping around the sailor

parts.note: to wash is to bath, bathe
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor taking a bath outdoors, in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wabash is a river of the US Midwest, flowing through Indiana to the Ohio.

clue.text: Setter's upward stroke blocks shot — pity!

indicators.note: the middle pieces block the shot word by sitting inside it

parts.note: a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: in a down clue going upward means the letters read backwards

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: my
a pat is a light stroke

explanation.surface: A tennis or cricket scene: an upward stroke from the setter blocks a shot, a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upward' turns MY into YM; YM plus PAT go inside SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy is fellow feeling for someone's misfortune, much the same as pity.

clue.text: Old copper has piano from East Enders sweetheart's scratched

indicators.note: a name scratched from a list is struck off, so these letters are removed

parts.note: joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (pianner), the speech of London's East End
jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A retired policeman owns the piano whose lover's name has been scratched off, an EastEnders soap storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Enders' looks like the BBC soap EastEnders but points to Cockney slang. 'scratched' removes JO from JOANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a copper coin of British India, worth one sixteenth of a rupee, now obsolete.

clue.text: Finishing off each can, dog's thrown up

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down clue thrown up means the letters are sent upward, read backwards

parts.note: the pug is a small dog breed

explanation.surface: A dog wolfs down each can of food and then is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' turns PUG into GUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating up means consuming completely, so finishing off a meal or a resource.

clue.text: General hospital getting a soldier upset

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so the letters read upwards in reverse

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A general in hospital with a distressed soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GI into IG.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Haig was the British field marshal commanding on the Western Front in the First World War.

clue.text: Building entrance unknown for a long time

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters of entrance are assembled in a new order

parts.note: y is one of the mathematician's unknowns, x, y and z

explanation.surface: A building's entrance has been a mystery for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenary is a hundred years, a long time, and the anniversary this puzzle marks.

clue.text: African natives from city in the way of …

parts.note: NY is New York
a la, French, means in the manner or style of

explanation.surface: Native Africans who come from a city, in the manner of something continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this surface on into 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope native to southern Africa; the plural is also nyala.

clue.text: … repairing outer road

indicators.note: a repair puts things back together differently, so the letters of outer are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 10 across: in the manner of mending a ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or course travelled, so a road.

clue.text: A prince's fruit and gin cocktail turning up

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A prince's fruity gin cocktail arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning up and appearing both mean arriving or coming into view.

clue.text: National Front of Belfast tense with Irish revolutionary

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
revolutionary means turning over, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: The far-right National Front in Belfast, tense alongside an Irish revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Front' reads as the party but the definition is just 'National'. 'revolutionary' shuffles T and IRISH into RITISH.
explanation.definitionFit: British is a nationality, and a British national is a citizen of the UK.

clue.text: President's withholding the last of human remains

indicators.note: withholding means keeping something back, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Biden's, belonging to Joe Biden, US President

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A president keeping some human remains to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a noun (human remains) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is to stay or wait, so bides means remains.

clue.text: Start getting judge to sit astride horse

indicators.note: the judge sits astride, legs either side, so the horse goes inside

parts.note: a trier is one who tries a case, a judge
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A judge being made to ride a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigger is what sets something off, its start; as a verb it also means to start.

clue.text: Shut up! Setter's dug around issue

parts.note: Setter's is setter is, I'm

indicators.note: the dug word goes around the issue word

parts.note: pried means dug or prised out
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: The setter, told to shut up, has been digging around an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like an order but is a definition: shut up, put away. 'around' puts SON inside PRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shut up is to be locked away, confined, like a prisoner.

clue.text: Fabric Raymond gets removed from boards

indicators.note: the person removed from boards is the managing director, MD, who sits on the board, so those letters come out of Raymond

explanation.surface: An actor named Raymond is taken off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' suggests the stage, but means company boards: their managing director, MD, is what leaves RAYMOND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a man-made textile fibre from cellulose, an artificial silk.

clue.text: Shop around hot city

indicators.note: the shop word goes around the hot letter

parts.note: a deli is a shop
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A delicatessen in a hot city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the city that holds New Delhi, India's capital.

clue.text: Inclined to introduce the head of religious education

indicators.note: the inclined word introduces, takes in, the letter

parts.note: leaning means inclined

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone keen to bring in a new head of religious education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious education' reads as the school subject, but only 'education' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the acquiring of knowledge, education.

clue.text: Might sound like Roman from successful period

indicators.note: says the next word is said aloud and gives the answer by its sound

parts.note: de is Latin, the Romans' language, for from

explanation.surface: A Roman's arrival perhaps, from a successful time.
explanation.definitionFit: One's day is a time of success or prominence, as in had their day.

clue.text: Means of staining poor-quality trousers, rather tight in front

indicators.note: trousers is the verb, to pocket, so the poor-quality word takes the others inside

parts.note: duff is British slang for useless, poor quality
rather! is an old British exclamation meaning yes

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: How shabby trousers got stained, a bit too tight at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun but is the verb, to pocket. YES and T go inside DUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is a substance used for dyeing, a means of staining fabric.

clue.text: Flower power shortly facing the end of hostility

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
opp. is short for opposite, facing

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Flower power, facing an end to hostilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower power' reads as the hippie slogan but splits after Flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The poppy is a red flower, worn in Britain to remember the war dead of 1918 and after.

clue.text: Key leader removed fencing — bitter shock?

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the trimmed key goes around the bitter word
the first letter of the key word is taken off

parts.note: a key is a low island, an isle
tart means sharp, bitter

explanation.surface: A fencing match where the key leader drops out, a bitter shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys. 'leader removed' turns ISLE into SLE, which goes around TART.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to shock or alarm someone suddenly.

clue.text: Confinement at home after making inventions

indicators.note: puts the home piece after the inventions piece

parts.note: lying is making things up, telling inventions
in means at home

explanation.surface: Confined to home after a burst of inventing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying-in is the old term for a mother's confinement in childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying-in is the period of bed rest around childbirth, once called confinement.

clue.text: Force restraint of member: not right

indicators.note: not means without, so the right letter is taken away

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle that restrains a limb, or member

explanation.surface: Holding back a member by force is not right.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a large military force, originally a Roman army unit; the British Legion is the veterans' charity.

clue.text: French painter dreadfully rueing …

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly, so the letters of rueing are in a bad state, rearranged

explanation.surface: A French artist bitterly regretting something, carried on in 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Narcisse Guérin was a French neoclassical painter, a teacher of Géricault and Delacroix.

clue.text: Diet of rolls — add sandwiches from French

indicators.note: the rolls and add words sandwich the French word, holding it between them

parts.note: buns are bread rolls
de is French for from
to tag on is to add

explanation.surface: A diet of bread rolls, with sandwiches added from the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' suggests food but is a parliament. DE goes in between BUN and STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is Germany's federal parliament; diet is a name for such a legislative assembly.

clue.text: … worst risks son's raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letter moves higher, nearer the start

parts.note: bets are risks taken

explanation.surface: Continuing 23 down: rueing the worst as a son's stakes go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' looks like the opposite of the answer, but as a verb it means defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to beat them, the same as to best them.

clue.text: One Direction getting brute to lose face

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a beast is a brute, a savage creature or person

explanation.surface: A member of boy band One Direction made to lose face as a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' suggests the boy band, but means one compass point. 'to lose face' takes B from BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, so one direction.

clue.text: Former student given finally more Guinness double stout

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil

indicators.note: takes the last letter of each of the following three words

explanation.surface: An old boy given more Guinness, a double measure of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double stout' looks like a beer order, but 'double' gives a letter and 'stout' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavily built person, so obese, very fat.

clue.text: Peer pressure ultimately applied against a heartless prince

indicators.note: the first piece is set next to, against, the rest
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of pressure
heartless means its middle letters are taken out

parts.note: a prince is a royal

explanation.surface: A peer put under pressure, set against a cruel prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the inside of ROYAL, leaving RL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Infilling suspect cavity

indicators.note: read as in filling: the word in goes into the middle of the suspect word

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspect, suspicious

explanation.surface: Someone filling in a suspect hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infilling' must be split as 'In filling': IN fills SUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity in bone, especially the air spaces in the skull.

clue.text: Fancier has best that is last of litter

parts.note: the flower of something is its best part
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A dog fancier owns the best pup, the last of the litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancier' suggests a breeder of dogs but is the comparative adjective, more ornate.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowery language or design is ornate, so the comparative means more elaborate, more fancy.
